title: Architecture Families & Evaluation
description: Study dense and mixture-of-experts models, sliding windows and cache policies, comparing model families responsibly, and capstone: a tiny language-model audit. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Dense and mixture-of-experts models
lessons.description: Separate active parameters, total parameters, routing overhead, and memory in a model comparison.
lessons.conceptOverview: Dense layers activate their parameters for each token; MoE routes tokens to a subset of expert networks. Active compute and total stored parameters are different quantities. Routing balance, expert communication, and capacity policies influence real performance.
lessons.whyItMatters: MoE can reduce active compute without reducing total parameter storage proportionally.

lessons.title: Sliding windows and cache policies
lessons.description: Compare full attention and windowed attention on a distant-evidence task.
lessons.conceptOverview: Windowed attention limits which prior tokens some layers can access. This changes attention and cache requirements but may affect tasks needing distant evidence. Mixed local/global architectures require layer-specific accounting rather than one universal full-context cache formula.
lessons.whyItMatters: Cache accounting must reflect the attention policy of each layer.

lessons.title: Comparing model families responsibly
lessons.description: Build a release-specific comparison table for two checkpoints and mark undocumented fields as unknown.
lessons.conceptOverview: A family name is not a complete model specification. Record the exact release, architecture, tokenizer, license, supported modalities, and evaluation settings. Compare dense and MoE models under a shared workload and resource budget instead of relying on headline parameter counts.

lessons.title: Capstone: a tiny language-model audit
lessons.description: Deliver a tokenizer report, training configuration, evaluation set, and analysis of three generation failures.
lessons.conceptOverview: Train or inspect a small next-token model with a fixed tokenizer, explicit data split, and reproducible settings. Report loss, generated examples, contamination checks, and failure cases. Small-scale experiments teach pipeline mechanics without establishing how a large model will behave.
lessons.whyItMatters: Separate verification of pipeline mechanics from claims about large-model capability.
